It does not verify that the target reported its citations, retrieved context, refusals, or escalations honestly. Grounding identifiers are checked against the context the target claims to have retrieved. A dishonest target is out of scope.
It does not evaluate a foundation model in the abstract. It evaluates one feature in its context: prompts, retrieval, guardrails, and routing, as deployed.
It does not measure answer quality, helpfulness, readability, accessibility, latency, or cost.

It does not establish coverage beyond the cases that ran. Attack classes, languages, populations, and scenarios absent from the case files are untested, and the counts in this pack are the whole of the claim.
A passing run says the declared cases passed at the declared thresholds, against this target, at this revision. It says nothing about untested inputs.
It does not replace human review or red-teaming. It is the fixture that keeps red-team findings regression-tested after the humans go home.
clean_run_caveat: A clean run is not by itself evidence that the gates work. The harness ships a deliberately breakable toy target and a paired test per gate that injects the defect the gate exists to catch and asserts the gate fails. Ask for those results alongside this pack.

cases.observed: The endpoint passed reachability checks: its /metadata path returned an HTTP 2xx response over HTTPS from all three vantage points tested, though all three vantages were on a single network (github-actions), so this represents one network's view sampled three times rather than three independent networks. The endpoint responded to the /metadata request in 958 ms (median across the three vantage points), completing the capabilities interaction that FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) requires a server to support. The CapabilityStatement — the machine-readable document a FHIR server publishes to describe what it supports — declares fhirVersion as '4.0.1', satisfying the requirement that this field be present; the FHIR specification marks fhirVersion as a mandatory (1..1) element. The CapabilityStatement does not include a software name or version. The FHIR specification defines an optional software block with a mandatory name child element, so while omitting the entire block is permitted, its absence means clients cannot identify the software platform behind this endpoint from the published document. The CapabilityStatement lists 22 resource types, and all 22 document their supported interactions. The FHIR specification states that "Servers SHALL specify what resource types and operations are supported" in their CapabilityStatement. The CapabilityStatement references US Core, CARIN, and Da Vinci implementation guide profiles in its instantiates and supportedProfile fields. US Core (the US Core Implementation Guide) "defines the minimum constraints on the FHIR resources to create the US Core Profiles" and establishes a floor for interoperability. A SMART App Launch discovery document was found and judged complete. SMART (Substitutable Medical Applications, Reusable Technologies) App Launch requires that "FHIR endpoints requiring authorization SHALL serve a JSON document at the location formed by appending /.well-known/smart-configuration to their base URL," and the CapabilityStatement also declares an OAuth/SMART security service, satisfying both discovery mechanisms.

El endpoint respondió al recurso /metadata con un código HTTP 2xx sobre HTTPS, lo que confirma que está disponible. Según la especificación FHIR R4, esta interacción recupera la información sobre las capacidades del servidor. La verificación de disponibilidad se realizó desde tres puntos de medición, pero todos pertenecen a una sola red (github-actions); no representa tres redes independientes. El tiempo de respuesta mediano fue de 958 ms. La especificación FHIR indica que la interacción se ejecuta mediante un comando HTTP GET al endpoint /metadata. El CapabilityStatement (documento que describe las capacidades del servidor FHIR — Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) declara la versión FHIR '4.0.1'. El campo fhirVersion es obligatorio según la especificación, con cardinalidad 1..1. El CapabilityStatement no incluye el nombre ni la versión del software. El elemento software es opcional en la especificación, pero su campo name es obligatorio si el bloque software está presente; al estar ausente, los clientes no pueden identificar el software que sustenta el endpoint. El CapabilityStatement declara 22 tipos de recursos y documenta las interacciones soportadas para cada uno de ellos. La especificación FHIR indica que los servidores deben especificar qué tipos de recursos y operaciones son compatibles. El documento declara perfiles de US Core, CARIN y Da Vinci en los campos CapabilityStatement.instantiates y rest.resource.supportedProfile. US Core es una guía de implementación basada en FHIR R4 que define restricciones mínimas sobre los recursos para promover la interoperabilidad. El endpoint publica un documento de descubrimiento SMART (Smart App Launch es el estándar que define cómo las aplicaciones obtienen autorización OAuth para acceder a datos FHIR) en la ruta /.well-known/smart-configuration, y el documento está completo. La especificación SMART exige que los endpoints que requieren autorización sirvan ese documento JSON en esa ubicación. El CapabilityStatement declara el servicio de seguridad OAuth/SMART en el campo rest.security.service, lo que permite a los clientes descubrir el mecanismo de autenticación requerido antes de realizar operaciones.

The reachability check attempted to reach the endpoint's /metadata path from three vantage points, all on the github-actions network, and received HTTP 401 responses each time; because only one network was used, the run cannot determine whether the endpoint is fully down or simply does not answer requests from that network. Because the /metadata path was not successfully reached, no latency measurement was possible, and the endpoint scored 0 out of 100 points for reachability. FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) R4 requires that applications return a resource describing server functionality when the /metadata path is requested; specifically, "Applications SHALL return a resource that describes the functionality of the server end-point." Because no /metadata response was retrieved, no CapabilityStatement — the structured document that lists which resource types and interactions a FHIR server supports — could be examined, so the transparency dimension was not observed and received no score. The FHIR specification notes that servers requiring authentication should still return a CapabilityStatement before authentication or authorization is performed; the HTTP 401 response observed here means that condition could not be confirmed from the published documents retrieved in this run. Because no CapabilityStatement was retrieved, the interoperability readiness dimension — which would assess things such as supported profiles and resource types — was also not observed and received no score. The overall grade for this run is "not observed" because the single network used could not reach the endpoint; a future run from additional networks would be needed to distinguish a fully unavailable endpoint from one that is network-restricted.

Durante esta ejecución, el programa intentó acceder al endpoint en la ruta /metadata desde tres puntos de red distintos, todos dentro de la red 'github-actions', y en ninguno obtuvo respuesta exitosa; el resultado fue HTTP 401. Por este motivo, la dimensión de accesibilidad (reachability) recibió 0 de 100 puntos posibles. La especificación FHIR R4 (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources, versión 4) exige que las aplicaciones devuelvan un recurso que describa las funciones del servidor al recibir una solicitud GET a /metadata. Según la especificación: "Applications SHALL return a resource that describes the functionality of the server end-point." Debido a que el endpoint respondió con HTTP 401 desde todas las vantajas probadas, esta ejecución no puede distinguir si el servidor estaba caído o si simplemente no responde a la red utilizada. La latencia no pudo medirse. El CapabilityStatement (recurso FHIR que describe las capacidades de un servidor, como los tipos de recursos e interacciones que soporta) no fue recuperado en ningún punto de red durante esta ejecución. Por ello, las dimensiones de transparencia (transparency) e interoperabilidad (interop) figuran como 'no observadas', lo que significa que la verificación no pudo ejecutarse, no que haya fallado. La especificación indica que todos los servidores deben soportar la interacción de capacidades: "All servers are required to support the capabilities interaction". Al no haberse podido recuperar el CapabilityStatement, no es posible confirmar en esta ejecución si el endpoint cumple con este requisito. La especificación también señala que, aunque se requiera autenticación, el servidor debería retornar un CapabilityStatement antes de completar el proceso de autenticación o autorización. El HTTP 401 recibido impidió verificar si este comportamiento estaba implementado.

cases.observed: The endpoint's /metadata URL responded with an HTTP 2xx status code over HTTPS from all three vantage points tested, earning full marks for reachability. FHIR — Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources — defines this endpoint as the standard way to discover a server's capabilities: "The capabilities interaction retrieves the information about a server's capabilities - which portions of this specification it supports." All three vantage points were hosts on a single network (github-actions), so the reachability check reflects one network's view sampled three times, not three independent networks. The median response time for /metadata was 562 ms across those three samples. The endpoint's CapabilityStatement — the machine-readable document that describes what a FHIR server supports — declares FHIR version 4.0.1. The specification requires this field: "fhirVersion value='[code]'/><!-- 1..1 FHIR Version the system supports". The CapabilityStatement also declares both a software name and a software version. The specification's structure provides dedicated fields for these: "A name the software is known by" and "Version covered by this statement". Three resource types are declared in the CapabilityStatement, and all three fully document their supported interactions. The specification states that "Servers SHALL specify what resource types and operations are supported" — this endpoint satisfies that requirement for every resource it lists. The interoperability check for standard profile alignment failed. Three profile canonicals are declared in rest.resource.profile, but none of them match US Core, CARIN, or Da Vinci profiles. US Core is an implementation guide that defines "the expected FHIR capabilities and requirements of the US Core Servers and Clients"; without a recognized profile, automated systems cannot confirm alignment to those shared data standards. A SMART App Launch discovery document was found and is complete, and an OAuth/SMART security service is declared in the CapabilityStatement. SMART (Substitutable Medical Applications and Reusable Technologies) requires that "FHIR endpoints requiring authorization SHALL serve a JSON document at the location formed by appending /.well-known/smart-configuration to their base URL"; this endpoint meets that requirement.

El endpoint respondió al path /metadata con un código HTTP 2xx sobre HTTPS, lo cual cumple con la forma en que FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) define la interacción de capacidades del servidor. El tiempo de respuesta medido fue de 562 ms como mediana; sin embargo, las tres mediciones provienen de hosts en una sola red (github-actions), por lo que no representan tres redes independientes. El documento publicado declara la versión FHIR '4.0.1', junto con el nombre y la versión del software. El CapabilityStatement (declaración de capacidades del servidor) reserva campos específicos para esa información: el elemento fhirVersion es obligatorio (cardinalidad 1..1) y los elementos de software como name y version son opcionales pero están presentes. El CapabilityStatement declara 3 tipos de recursos y documenta las interacciones de los 3. La especificación indica que los servidores deben especificar qué tipos de recursos y operaciones son compatibles. Ninguno de los 3 perfiles canónicos declarados en el CapabilityStatement corresponde a US Core, CARIN ni Da Vinci. US Core es una guía de implementación que define perfiles de referencia para interoperabilidad en EE. UU. La especificación señala que los servidores deberían especificar perfiles para cada tipo de recurso, pero los perfiles publicados no coinciden con los estándares buscados, lo que resultó en 0/40 puntos en esta verificación. El endpoint publica un documento de descubrimiento SMART (/.well-known/smart-configuration) completo. SMART (Substitutable Medical Apps, Reusable Technologies) es el marco de autorización sobre OAuth utilizado con FHIR. La especificación requiere que los endpoints que exigen autorización sirvan ese documento JSON. El servicio de seguridad OAuth/SMART está declarado dentro del CapabilityStatement, en el campo rest.security.service, que acepta valores como 'SMART-on-FHIR'.

The endpoint is reachable: its /metadata path returned an HTTP 2xx response over HTTPS from all three vantage points used in the test. FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) specifies that GET [base]/metadata is how a server's capabilities are retrieved. All three vantage points were hosts on a single GitHub Actions network, so the reachability check reflects one network's view sampled three times, not three independent networks. The /metadata endpoint responded with a median latency of 1,593 ms across the three vantage points, earning full points for response time. The CapabilityStatement (the document a FHIR server publishes to describe what it supports) declares FHIR version 4.0.1, software name, software version, and 146 resource types — each with their supported interactions documented. The specification requires that 'fhirVersion' be present as a mandatory field. Although 147 profile canonicals are declared in the CapabilityStatement, none of them match US Core, CARIN, or Da Vinci profiles. US Core (a widely used implementation guide for US healthcare data exchange) defines expected FHIR capabilities through its own CapabilityStatements, and the absence of any US Core profile reference means interoperability with US Core-based systems is not demonstrated by these published documents. No OAuth security service is declared in the CapabilityStatement's security section. The specification allows servers to advertise security services such as 'OAuth' or 'SMART-on-FHIR' in that field. The check for a SMART App Launch discovery document at /.well-known/smart-configuration was not observed on this run, so whether the endpoint publishes one is unknown. SMART App Launch (a specification for authorizing third-party apps with FHIR servers) requires that endpoints needing authorization serve a JSON document at that path.

El servidor respondió correctamente a la ruta /metadata con un código HTTP 2xx sobre HTTPS, lo que confirma que el punto de conexión es accesible. Sin embargo, la prueba se realizó desde tres hosts dentro de una sola red (github-actions), no desde tres redes independientes. El tiempo de respuesta de /metadata fue de 1 593 ms (mediana de los tres puntos de observación). La especificación FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) describe esta interacción como una petición HTTP GET a [base]/metadata que devuelve información sobre las capacidades del servidor. El documento publicado declara la versión de FHIR como '4.0.1'. El recurso CapabilityStatement (documento que describe las capacidades del servidor) exige el campo fhirVersion con cardinalidad 1..1, es decir, es obligatorio y debe aparecer exactamente una vez. El CapabilityStatement declara el nombre y la versión del software. La especificación define estos campos dentro del elemento software, donde el nombre (name) es obligatorio (1..1) y la versión (version) es opcional (0..1). El CapabilityStatement declara 146 tipos de recursos y documenta las interacciones admitidas para cada uno de ellos. La especificación indica que los servidores deben especificar qué tipos de recursos y operaciones son compatibles. Se declararon 147 perfiles en el CapabilityStatement, pero ninguno corresponde a US Core, CARIN ni Da Vinci. US Core es una guía de implementación que define perfiles de recursos y declara sus requisitos de conformidad; sus páginas de conformidad describen las capacidades esperadas de los servidores y clientes. No se declaró ningún servicio de seguridad OAuth en el CapabilityStatement. Además, la verificación de /.well-known/smart-configuration (documento JSON que los puntos de conexión que requieren autorización deben publicar según SMART App Launch) no se ejecutó en esta evaluación, por lo que se desconoce si está disponible.

harness_properties.enforces: A harness property rather than a gate: a deliberately breakable toy target ships in-repo, and every built-in gate has a paired test that injects the defect the gate exists to catch and asserts the gate fails. One of those defects removes the answer itself, and every built-in gate is demonstrated failing against it, so no built-in gate can be passed by a target that says nothing. A gate the toy cannot exercise, such as one that needs a model, is outside this doctrine and the pack reports it as unmapped rather than covered. A check that has never failed is not evidence of health.

framework_references.locator: Risk Assessment Part 1, Safeguard Level scale
framework_references.informs: The scale runs from Not Identified to Fully Identified. The difference between an identified safeguard and a working one is demonstrability, which is what the failure demonstrations provide.

framework_references.locator: Risk Assessment Part 2, Details of Transparency, item (b)
framework_references.informs: Auditability of the system: a reviewer can break the toy and watch each built-in gate catch it, rather than trusting that the gates work.

harness_properties.disclosure_support: Makes the evidence pack inspectable by a skeptical reviewer: the disclosure can invite the reviewer to run the failure demonstrations themselves.

mapping.informs_meaning: 'Informs' means the gate produces runnable, repeatable evidence a state entity or vendor can attach when answering that item. It never means the gate satisfies the item by itself, and it never means the item has been reviewed by anyone.

Defines 'Material Impact / Materially Impacts', the materiality trigger for contractor disclosure.

Carries the procurement duties: written contractor notice when GenAI is a deliverable or materially impacts one, completion of SIMM 5305-F before award, and CDT consultation when the assessed risk is Moderate or High. A vendor making that written disclosure can attach a Gauntlet run as the testing evidence behind it.

States that GenAI contract language is incorporated into the state's standard information technology provisions, and that additional GenAI clauses apply when a SIMM 5305-F indicates Moderate or High risk and a CDT consultation confirms that level.
